> Premium, conversion-focused website theme for local service businesses — HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical, cleaning and remodeling contractors. One reusable design system, multiple industry demos, lead-generation layouts, and GHL integration guides.

**Repository positioning:** Premium GoHighLevel website theme for local service businesses, featuring reusable components, conversion-focused landing pages, lead-generation forms, responsive layouts and GHL implementation documentation.

---

## Introduction

**ServicePro** is a premium, conversion-focused GoHighLevel website theme built for local service businesses. Rather than publishing a single static template, ServicePro is engineered as a **reusable design system** — one architecture that spins up polished, high-converting websites for any local service industry.

The repository includes **three complete industry demonstrations** (HVAC, Plumbing, Roofing) that share the same components, layout patterns and conversion structure, each re-themed instantly with its own brand palette, copy, services, testimonials, pricing and FAQ.

This project serves two purposes:

1. **A ready-to-customize starting point** for agencies and freelancers building GoHighLevel websites for service businesses.
2. **A portfolio asset** demonstrating Muhammad Hamid's GHL development, conversion design and marketing automation capabilities.

### Value proposition

- **One design system, many industries** — add a new industry by editing a single data file.
- **Conversion-focused** — every section is designed to generate qualified leads.
- **Production-grade** — semantic HTML, accessibility, SEO metadata, responsive layouts.
- **GHL-ready** — documented integration points for forms, CRM, calendars, pipelines and workflows.
- **Honest** — demo content is clearly labeled as fictional samples; no fake ratings in structured data.

---

## Live demo

A hosted preview of the ServicePro theme is available. Use the industry switcher in the header to toggle between HVAC, Plumbing and Roofing demos live.

> **Note:** This repository contains the external Next.js preview of the design system. The live GoHighLevel implementation is delivered as native GHL elements (custom HTML/CSS sections, GHL forms, calendars, pipelines and workflows) via the documented implementation process in [docs/GHL-IMPLEMENTATION.md](docs/GHL-IMPLEMENTATION.md).

---

## Features

### Conversion optimization

- Strong homepage headline with clear value proposition
- Prominent phone and contact CTAs in the sticky header
- Free quote request form with validation and success/error states
- Booking and consultation CTAs throughout the page
- Trust-building testimonials (clearly labeled as demo content)
- "Why choose us" section with credibility points
- Before-and-after project showcase gallery
- Service coverage area pages
- FAQ accordion addressing common objections
- Emergency service CTA banner
- Repeated conversion opportunities across every section
- Sticky mobile CTA bar (Call + Free quote) — always one tap away
- Floating WhatsApp hiring button with pre-filled inquiry messages

# marvis-portfolio

Production site for **Muhammad Hamid** — Digital Marketing Head moving into AI automation
engineering. Live at **https://marvis.web.app**.

A dependency-free static site generator: Node 20, ES modules, zero npm packages. The build reads a
committed snapshot of a GitHub "master record" and renders 38 routes, then a validator gates the
output on links, SEO, and contact policy before anything reaches Firebase Hosting.

## Why it exists

The portfolio is generated, not hand-written. Facts about projects come from
`hamids-ai-automations/github-profile-master-record` (`MASTER_DATABASE.json`), so the site cannot
drift from the repositories it describes. A daily workflow refreshes the snapshot, and any change to
the record hash triggers a rebuild and deploy.

## Page inventory

| Section | Routes |
| --- | --- |
| Home | `/` |
| Work index | `/projects/` |
| Projects | 19 curated case pages (`/projects/<slug>/`) |
| Writing index | `/articles/` |
| Articles | 4 long-form pieces (`/articles/<slug>/`) |
| Services index | `/services/` |
| Services | 6 offers (`/services/<slug>/`) |
| About / Contact | `/about/`, `/contact/` |
| Legal | `/privacy/`, `/terms/` |
| Machine surfaces | `/sitemap.xml` (35 URLs), `/robots.txt`, `/llms.txt`, `/data/projects.json`, `/site.webmanifest`, `/404.html` |

## Quick start

```bash
npm run build      # render dist/
npm run validate   # gate the output
npm test           # 30 unit tests
npm run serve      # preview at http://localhost:5000 with Firebase-like routing
npm run ci         # build + validate + test — run before every push
```

No install step is required: the project has no dependencies.

## Structure

```
data/          committed snapshot of the master record (source of truth)
scripts/       sync, build entry, validate gate, local server
src/lib/       data parsing, normalisation, model, layout, SEO, markdown
src/pages/     one renderer per page family
src/content/   site copy, services, articles, curated project overrides
src/templates/ cards and shared components
src/styles.css the entire stylesheet
tests/         node:test suites
dist/          generated output (never edit)
```

## Content rules

- Every project claim traces to the master record or to a curated override that restates a verified
  field from it.
- WhatsApp `+923167417135` is the only contact channel: no forms, no email links, no phone-call CTAs.

# LeadFlow Sentinel

[![CI](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%20%7C%203.11%20%7C%203.12-blue)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel/blob/main/pyproject.toml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE)
[![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-101%20passing-brightgreen)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel/tree/main/tests)

**Read-only CRM health, lead-to-booking monitoring and revenue-leakage detection for GoHighLevel (HighLevel) agencies.**

LeadFlow Sentinel audits a GoHighLevel sub-account snapshot, scores its health, and reports the exact leads, opportunities and bookings where money is leaking — with the evidence attached, not a vague "your CRM could be better".

- Zero-dependency Python core. No account, no API key, no dashboard needed to get a first report.
- Read-only by design: nothing in the CRM is created, updated or deleted.
- Deterministic: the same snapshot always produces the same score, so numbers in a client proposal cannot drift overnight.
- AI is optional and fenced: narratives are only accepted when every claim traces back to a finding.

```bash
python -m leadflow_sentinel demo --out demo-audit.json
```

That writes a full audit of a synthetic agency account (52 contacts, 24 opportunities, 15 webhook events, 12 planted defect classes) in under a second.

---

## Why this exists

GoHighLevel agencies do not lose money because a dashboard is missing. They lose it because:

1. **Leads arrive and nobody follows up.** A form fill creates a contact; no opportunity, no call, no appointment. The lead goes cold inside 72 hours.
2. **The same person exists three times.** One record from a Facebook lead form, one from a website form, one imported from a spreadsheet. Reporting counts them as three leads; the follow-up automation fires on the wrong one.
3. **Bookings are never confirmed.** An appointment sits in `pending` forever; the show-up rate collapses and nobody notices until the month ends.
4. **Webhooks fail silently.** HighLevel retries, times out or pauses a subscription; the workflow that was supposed to run simply did not run.

Each of those is measurable from data the account already holds. LeadFlow Sentinel measures them, prices them in severity, and tells the operator which specific records to fix first.

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel
cd leadflow-sentinel

# 1. Prove the detectors fire on known planted defects
python -m leadflow_sentinel selftest

# 2. Audit the synthetic demo account, write a JSON report
python -m leadflow_sentinel demo --out demo-audit.json

# 3. Audit the demo account and write a client-ready Markdown report
python -m leadflow_sentinel demo --out demo-audit.md

# 4. Audit your own snapshot (see docs/GHL-INTEGRATION.md for the shape)
python -m leadflow_sentinel audit --dataset s

# ghl-automation-engine

HighLevel (GoHighLevel) integration engine for teams that put automations in
production and cannot afford them to be quietly wrong.

The GoHighLevel ecosystem already has a 900-tool MCP server. Tool *count* is not
the bottleneck. Reliability is. This project is deliberately narrow: it makes the
failure modes visible instead of silent.

## The four failures this exists to prevent

| Failure | What it looks like in production | What this library does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Silent pagination truncation | Page 2 of 5 fails, the caller returns page 1, a downstream workflow treats 100 contacts as "all contacts" and archives the rest | Cursor walking is exhaustive by contract: you get a `Collection` with an honest `complete` flag, or a `GhlPartialResultError` carrying what was collected |
| Refresh-token stampede | 12 concurrent workers see an expired token, all refresh, the provider rotates the refresh token, 11 calls return `invalid_grant`, the integration hard-fails | Single-flight refresh under a lock with a double-checked expiry, and the rotated token is persisted before the lock is released |
| PII in logs | A debug line logs the contact upsert body and every email address lands in the log aggregator | Recursive redaction of credentials, emails, and phone numbers before any log record is emitted |
| Untestable integrations | Every test needs a live sub-account and a private token, so there are no tests | An offline mock server with fault injection; the whole suite runs on a clean machine in seconds |
| Webhook replays processed twice | A captured delivery is resent, or a platform retry arrives after a partial write, and the contact is created or the invoice is paid twice | Signature + timestamp window + an atomic seen-set; a duplicate returns `200` with `process=false`, so the sender stops retrying and your code does not run again |

## Install

```bash
git clone <this repo>
cd ghl-automation-engine
python -m pytest
```

No dependencies. The runtime uses only the standard library, so `pytest` is the
only thing you need, and CI needs no Docker and no network.

## Quickstart

```python
from ghl_client import ContactsResource, GhlClient, PrivateIntegrationToken

client = GhlClient(
    PrivateIntegrationToken(token="pit-..."),
    location_id="loc_...",
)

contacts = ContactsResource(client)
result = contacts.search(query="@example.com")

if not result.complete:
    raise SystemExit(f"refusing to act on {len(result)} of an unknown total")

for contact in result.items:
    ...
```

Idempotent writes:

```python
# Replaying this call does not create a duplicate contact.
contacts.upsert({"email": "jane@example.com"}, idempotency_key="sync-run-2026-11-21")
```

## Webhooks

```python
from ghl_webhooks import Receiver

receiver = Receiver(["whsec_..."])

def handle_delivery(headers, raw_body):
    intake = receiver.handle(headers, raw_body)
    if intake.should_process:
        dispatch(intake.event)      # a real, first-time, verified event
    return intake.http_status, {"status": intake.status.value}
```

readme.excerpt:
# Gemini Agent Reliability Kit (GAR Kit)

[![ci](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-reliability-kit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-reliability-kit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%20%7C%203.11%20%7C%203.12-blue)](pyproject.toml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE)

Most Gemini agent failures are not "the model is dumb". They are concrete, boring, and repeatable:

- the model picks the right tool but drops a required argument,
- it returns JSON that is 95% correct and unusable,
- it retries four times with the same backoff and burns your quota,
- one case in the suite takes 9 seconds and nobody notices until it is in production.

GAR Kit turns a handful of labelled cases into a **report card** that names the failure, on the case, in CI,
before your users find it. Zero dependencies, no network or API key needed for the default path.

```
GAR Kit report card  suite=smoke  model=mock-1  cases=6
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ID                  PASS  SCHEMA  TOOLS  ARGS  RETRY  LATENCY  COST($)
tool-basic          no    ok      ok     ok    FAIL   ok       0.000000
schema-json         no    ok      ok     ok    FAIL   ok       0.000000
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
pass rate 0.0%  (gate 90.0%)  -> FAIL
failures by check: retry=6

EVIDENCE
  tool-basic / retry: 5 attempts exceeded budget of 3
  schema-json / retry: 5 attempts exceeded budget of 3
```

## Quickstart

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-reliability-kit
cd gemini-agent-reliability-kit
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/Scripts/activate   # Windows; use .venv/bin/activate on macOS/Linux
pip install -e ".[dev]"

gar run --suite suites/smoke.json --provider mock --report reports/smoke.md
```

Add `--fail-on-gate` to turn the gate into an exit code: `1` when the gate is missed, `0` when it passes. Without
the flag a failing card still exits `0`, which is what you want for an exploratory run and not what you want in CI.
The mock provider is deterministic: same suite in, same card out, no credentials.

## Running against a real model

```bash
# PowerShell
$env:GEMINI_API_KEY = "...."
gar run --suite suites/smoke.json --provider gemini --model gemini-2.0-flash `
        --report reports/gemini-smoke.md --json reports/gemini-smoke.json --fail-on-gate
```

The Gemini provider uses the plain REST endpoint over `urllib` — no SDK, no transitive dependency tree.
It reports what actually happened: `attempts`, `backoff_ms`, `usageMetadata` token counts. Nothing is estimated
except the price table, and if the response carries no usage metadata the cost is reported as `0`, never invented.

## What gets checked

| check | question it answers | failure looks like |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | Does the structured output satisfy the declared subset of JSON Schema? | missing key, wrong type, unparsable JSON |
| `tool_call` | Did the model pick the expected tool (and not a dangerous one)? | `delete_everything` instead of `get_weather` |
| `args` | Did the call carry every required argument with the expected value? | `{}` sent to a tool that needs `city` |
| `retry` | Did the turn stay inside the attempt budget with growing backoff? | 5 attempts, flat 40 ms spacing |
| `latency` | Did the case stay inside `max_latency_ms`? | p95 regression nobody caught in review |

Every failure carries a one-line evidence string naming the case and the check, so a red CI job tells you what to
fix instead of just that something is wrong.

```json
{
  "name": "smoke",
  "gate": {"min_pass_rate": 0.9},
  "cases": [
    {
      "id": "tool-basic",
      "prompt": "What is the weather in Lahore right now?",
      "tools": [{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties

readme.excerpt:
envscope: zero-dependency CLI that audits .env files against .env.example and a JSON schema, never printing secret values.

## Features
- Drift detection (missing, extra, empty, duplicate keys)
- Type validation: string, int, float, bool, port, url, email, pattern, choices
- Duplicate detection
- Secret-aware (values flagged secret are never printed)
- CI-friendly (--json, --sarif, stable exit codes)
- SARIF 2.1.0 export for GitHub code scanning
- Zero dependencies (Python 3.9+)
- Fast (parses thousands of keys in milliseconds)

## Requirements
- Python 3.11 or newer
- macOS, Linux, or Windows

## Install
```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/envscope.git
cd envscope
python -m pip install -e .
```

## Usage
```bash
envscope check [--env .env --example .env.example --schema envscope.json --strict --json --sarif PATH --quiet --no-color]
envscope init --example .env.example --out envscope.json
envscope version
```

## Schema format
envscope.json: `{"variables": {"APP_ENV":{"type":"string","choices":["development","staging","production"]},...}}`
Flat `{"PORT":"port"}` also accepted.

## CI example
```yaml
- name: Validate environment contract
  run: |
    python -m pip install -e .
    envscope check --strict --json > envscope-report.json
  env:
    PYTHONPATH: src
```

## SARIF / code scanning
`envscope check --sarif envscope.sarif` writes a SARIF 2.1.0 log next to the normal
output. Findings map to one rule per issue code (`parse`, `duplicate`, `missing`,
`empty`, `invalid`, `extra`) with error/warning levels, so GitHub code scanning can
group and annotate them inline on the offending dotenv line.

The log only contains key names, line numbers and envscope's own messages. Secret
values are never written to it, which is what makes it safe to upload as a build
artifact.

```yaml
- name: Validate environment contract
  run: |
    python -m pip install -e .
    envscope check --strict --sarif envscope.sarif
  env:
    PYTHONPATH: src
  continue-on-error: true

- name: Upload SARIF
  uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  with:
    sarif_file: envscope.sarif
    category: envscope
```

## Tests
42 tests, no dependencies. CI runs on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13.

## License
MIT

readme.excerpt:
# PinVault — Pinterest Image & Video Downloader

PinVault is a local-first Chrome extension (Manifest V3) for saving Pinterest images and **directly accessible** videos with the best available resolution, smart filenames, bulk download queues, duplicate detection, collections, and CSV/JSON inventory export.

**No build step, no runtime dependencies, vanilla JavaScript.** Request only the permissions it needs and never transmits your data.

> **Legal reminder:** Save only content you are authorized to save. Respect creator rights and applicable copyright law. PinVault does not bypass DRM, logins, CAPTCHAs, or rate limits.

## Features

- **Hover quick download** — a download button appears over Pinterest pins (home feed, boards, search, pin pages).
- **Popup quick download** — paste a pin URL (including `pin.it` short links) and download it directly.
- **Page scan** — collect media from the current board/search/pin page into the dashboard.
- **Bulk downloads** — bounded-concurrency queue (default 3), progress, pause, resume, cancel, and retry with backoff.
- **Filters & selection** — orientation, minimum dimensions, format, duplicate status; select all / deselect / individual selection with preview.
- **Highest accessible resolution** — picks the widest accessible CDN variant and excludes login-walled variants.
- **Smart naming** — configurable templates: `pinterest-title-001.jpg`, `board-name_pin-id.jpg`, `yyyy-mm-dd_pin-id.webp`; sanitized, path-traversal-safe filenames.
- **Duplicate prevention** — normalized media URLs and pin ids keep repeats out of your Downloads.
- **Collections** — save collected media records into named local collections.
- **History** — review past downloads, retry failures, clear independently of Chrome's download history.
- **CSV/JSON export** — media inventory with pin URL, dimensions, format, and status.
- **Light/dark/system theme**, keyboard-navigable, accessible UI.
- **Video support** — direct MP4/WebM downloads; segmented HLS and DRM-protected videos are explicitly marked unsupported (never bypassed).
- **Privacy** — local-first; one-click "Erase all PinVault data".

## Install (developer mode, load unpacked)

1. Download the release ZIP (`dist/pinvault-pinterest-downloader-1.0.0.zip`) and extract it, **or** clone the repository.
2. Open `chrome://extensions`.
3. Enable **Developer mode** (top-right).
4. Click **Load unpacked** and select the folder that contains `manifest.json` (the project root, e.g. `D:\pin extension\PinVault`).
5. Pin the PinVault toolbar icon. Visit a Pinterest board and hover a pin to test.

To repackage from source: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build.ps1`.

## Usage

### Quick download
- **Hover:** hover any pin → click the download button.
- **Popup:** click the PinVault toolbar icon → paste a pin URL → **Download**. The popup also shows the current page's media count, a mini queue, and recent history.

### Bulk download
1. Open the dashboard (`chrome://extensions` → PinVault → Details → Extension options, or right-click the toolbar icon → Options).
2. Go to **Collect** → **Scan current page** (or scroll and re-scan to capture lazy-loaded pins).
3. Filter and select media, then **Download selected**.
4. Watch progress in **Bulk downloads**; pause, cancel, retry as needed.

### Collections, history, exports
- **Collections:** create a named collection and add selected media records.
- **History:** review downloads, retry failed items, clear history.
- **Export:** export the current inventory as CSV or JSON.

| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `storage` | Store settings/history/queue/collections/duplicate index locally |
| `downloads` | Save media through Chrome's Downloads API |
| `activeTab` | Read the active Pinterest tab when you click the popup |
| Host: `*://*.pinterest.com/*`, `*://*.pinimg.com/*`, `https://pin.it/*` | Operate only on Pinterest and its media CDN |

Dynamic Schema Generator for WordPress

Automated, Production-Grade JSON-LD Schema.org Structured Data Engine with Elementor Integration

readme.excerpt:
# issuefit

Score a GitHub issue before you spend a weekend on it.

`issuefit` answers three separate questions with evidence from the repository itself, then refuses to
pretend they are one number:

| Output | Question it answers | Evidence used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `merged_pr_probability` | Will an outside PR actually get merged here? | external merge rate, median time-to-merge, open-issue load, contributor-friendly labels |
| `maintainer_responsiveness` | Is anyone awake on the other side? | days since last push, maintainer reply in this thread, discussion volume, review speed |
| `stack_match` | Is this near my Python / MCP / LLM / FastAPI / Docker stack? | repository language plus keyword evidence in title, body and labels |

The fit score is `0.50 * merged_pr_probability + 0.35 * maintainer_responsiveness + 0.15 * stack_match`,
minus penalties for a thread with no reproduction detail (`-8`) and a repository untouched for more than
30 days (`-10`). It is clamped to 0-100. Every point comes from a named rule in
[`src/issuefit/score.py`](src/issuefit/score.py), and the CLI prints those rules back as `reasons`.

## Verdicts

Ordered by how hard the blocker is, because a high score does not rescue a blocked issue:

1. `rejected-not-fixable` — `dependency dashboard`, `dependencies`, `stale`, `question`, `support` labels.
2. `blocked-competing-pr` — an open PR already cross-references the issue (checked via the timeline API).
3. `needs-reproduction` — labelled `bug` but the thread has no steps/stack trace/expected-vs-actual.
4. `qualified` — score is at or above 60 and none of the blockers apply.
5. `watch` — everything else.

## Install

```bash
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

## Run the demo (offline, no token)

```bash
issuefit demo
issuefit demo --json
```

The demo scores a bundled fixture whose payload shapes are copied from real GitHub API responses but
whose values are synthetic. It is a demonstration, not a benchmark.

## Score live issues

```bash
export ISSUEFIT_TOKEN=...            # or GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN; needs public read, repo read for private repos
issuefit score --repo example-org/ha-mcp --issue 3166
issuefit scan --query "mcp in:title is:issue is:open" --limit 15 --min-score 60 --out scored.json
```

`scan` writes the **full** scored list to `--out` (rejected and blocked issues included) and prints only
what clears `--min-score`, so nothing is silently dropped.

```console
$ issuefit demo
issuefit demo - fixture evaluated as of 2026-11-21T14:00:00+00:00 (no network, no token)

score  verdict               repo                        issue                                                     merge%  resp%  stack%
93.4   qualified             example-org/ha-mcp          #3166 [FEATURE] bulk entity update: optional compact r    94      90     100
76.8   blocked-competing-pr  example-org/agent-sdk       #7052 [Bug]: glob tool returns nothing for patterns wi    73      72     100
67.3   needs-reproduction    example-org/support-desk    #473 Problems connecting FastAPI app to the platform      92      41     100
66.1   rejected-not-fixable  example-org/design-system   #1204 Dependency Dashboard                                85      65      60

Top candidate reasoning:
  - repo baseline 40
  - external merges 6/8 (75%) -> +19
  - median merge 2.0h -> +20
  - 14 open issues -> +8
  - contributor-friendly label ['enhancement'] -> +7
  - pushed 0.1d ago -> +30
  - maintainer already replied -> +20
  - 4 comments -> +5
  - open-issue load 14 -> +15
  - review speed 2.0h -> +20
  - stack match 100% (weight 15%)
  - thread contains reproduction detail
```

## Design notes

- **Two stdlib-only layers.** `signals.py` derives facts, `score.py` turns facts into points. Anything
  that needs the network lives in `github.py`, so the scoring engine is testable as pure functions.
- **Injected clock.** `derive_signals(issue, now=...)` means freshness scoring never depends on the day
  the test runs.
- **Insiders are

readme.excerpt:
# Google Services MCP

A permission-controlled [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) gateway that gives AI agents scoped,
auditable access to **Google Drive, Sheets, Gmail, Calendar and Docs** — with OAuth scopes, a server-side permission
policy, mandatory confirmation for destructive actions, rate limiting and a JSONL audit trail.

The design goal is blunt: an agent should be able to *read* your workspace by default, and only *change* it when a human
operator deliberately widened the policy. The policy lives in the server, not in the prompt, so no amount of prompting
can talk its way past it.

```
agent ──MCP──▶ tool wrapper ──▶ 1. rate limit ──▶ 2. permission policy ──▶ 3. Google API
                                    │                                         │
                                    └── 4. redact + truncate ◀────────────────┘
                                                     │
                                                     └──▶ audit.jsonl
```

## Highlights

- **Default read-only.** `read_only` mode blocks every write/destructive tool before a network call is made.
- **Per-service, per-action flags.** `drive.share`, `gmail.send`, `calendar.delete`, … each have their own switch.
- **Two-key outbound email.** Sending requires `permissions.allow_email_send: true` *and* `gmail.send: true` *and*
  `confirm: true` on the call itself.
- **Dry-run by default.** Writes preview their effect unless the caller passes `dry_run: false`; deletions need
  `confirm: true` as well.
- **44 tools** across five services, each with an MCP `ToolSpec` (operation, policy key, scopes, annotations).
- **Untrusted content handling.** Gmail/Drive/Docs text is wrapped and control characters stripped before it reaches the
  model, so a malicious document cannot smuggle instructions.
- **Local file sandbox.** Drive upload/download are confined to `files.download_dir`; path traversal is rejected.
- **Audit without payloads.** `logs/audit.jsonl` records tool, service, outcome, duration, correlation id — never
  message bodies or tokens.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/google-services-mcp.git
cd google-services-mcp
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\activate            # Windows
# source .venv/bin/activate         # macOS / Linux
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

Requirements: Python 3.11+, an OAuth client (Desktop app) from Google Cloud Console with the Drive, Sheets, Gmail,
Calendar and Docs APIs enabled.

## Configure

```bash
cp config/config.example.yaml config/config.yaml
cp .env.example .env
```

Every flag in `permissions.services` maps to a policy key used by the tools. Widening one widens what the agent can do:

| Service | Policy keys | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `drive` | `read`, `create`, `update`, `upload`, `share`, `delete` | `delete` also needs `confirm=true` per call |
| `sheets` | `read`, `write`, `create`, `delete` | `delete` removes a whole sheet (irreversible) |
| `gmail` | `read`, `draft`, `send`, `modify`, `trash` | `send` needs `allow_email_send` + `confirm=true` |
| `calendar` | `read`, `create`, `update`, `delete` | deleting an event also needs `confirm=true` |
| `docs` | `read`, `create`, `update` | updates are append/insert/replace-text only |

`permissions.mode` adds a global gate on top: `read_only` (reads only), `read_write` (flag-driven), `restricted`
(only names in `allowed_tools`), `custom` (flags only, no mode-level short-circuit).

## Authorise

```bash
google-services-mcp auth login               # opens a browser, stores the refresh token
google-services-mcp auth login --console     # headless: paste the code
google-services-mcp auth login --write       # request write scopes too
google-services-mcp auth status              # token presence, expiry, granted scopes
google-services-mcp auth logout              # revoke at Google and delete locally
```

Tick the scopes you actually intend to use. A token that was granted read-only scopes can

readme.excerpt:
# Gemini Agent Automation Toolkit

[![tests](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-automation-toolkit/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-automation-toolkit/actions/workflows/tests.yml)
[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)

A small, modular Python toolkit for building **reliable** Google Gemini agents: validated tool
calling, Pydantic structured outputs, retries with backoff, human approval for sensitive actions,
multi-step workflows and redacted execution logging.

It is deliberately opinionated and dependency-light — a thin, testable layer over the official
[`google-genai`](https://github.com/googleapis/python-genai) SDK instead of another framework.

- Project page: **https://marvis.web.app/projects/gemini-agent-automation-toolkit.html**
- Repository: **https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-automation-toolkit**

---

## Why this toolkit

Most "Gemini wrapper" packages stop at a single API call. Real agents need the boring parts:
tools that validate their own arguments, outputs that fail loudly instead of silently, retries that
do not duplicate side effects, a human in the loop before anything destructive happens, and logs you
can hand to a security reviewer.

| Capability | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| Agent engine | `Agent(...).run(prompt)` with instructions, context, usage metadata and typed results |
| Tools | `@tool` decorator, JSON schema generation, argument validation, recursion and call limits |
| Structured output | Pydantic schemas validated on the way out, with explicit `StructuredOutputError` |
| Reliability | Exponential backoff with jitter, transient/permanent error classification, timeouts |
| Human approval | Policies, single-use tokens bound to arguments, expiry, safe failure when unavailable |
| Workflows | Ordered steps, state passing, per-step retries, approval checkpoints, execution history |
| Observability | Structured JSON or plain logs, secrets and API keys redacted, token usage recorded |

Everything is in-memory by design; nothing is persisted unless you persist it yourself.

## Install

```bash
pip install gemini-agent-toolkit
```

From source (development):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-automation-toolkit.git
cd gemini-agent-automation-toolkit
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\activate      # Windows
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

Python 3.10+ is required. The only runtime dependencies are `google-genai` and `pydantic` v2.

## Quick start

Set your key once (never commit it):

```bash
set GEMINI_API_KEY=your-key        # PowerShell: $env:GEMINI_API_KEY="your-key"
```

```python
from gemini_agent_toolkit import Agent

agent = Agent(
    name="Research Assistant",
    instructions="You are a helpful research assistant.",
)

result = agent.run("Explain how AI agents work in three sentences.")
print(result.output)
print(result.usage)  # token usage when the API reports it
```

## Tools

```python
from gemini_agent_toolkit import Agent, tool


@tool
def calculate_total(price: float, quantity: int) -> float:
    """Calculate a purchase total."""
    return price * quantity


agent = Agent(
    name="Shopping Assistant",
    instructions="Help users calculate totals.",
    tools=[calculate_total],
)

result = agent.run("Calculate the total for 5 items costing 20 each.")
```

The model proposes a tool call; the toolkit validates arguments against the generated schema,
executes the function, feeds the real result back to the model, and records the call. A proposal is
never reported as an executed call.

Useful decorator options:

```python
@tool(requires_approval=True, approval_reason="Deletes user data")
def delete_file(file_path: str) -> str: ...


@tool(idempotent=True, timeout=5.0, tags=("files",))
def read_file(file_path: str) ->

readme.excerpt:
# sarif-verify

Validate a SARIF 2.1.0 log **before** GitHub code scanning sees it.

`upload-sarif` fails late and vaguely: a `ruleIndex` that disagrees with
`ruleId` silently mislabels findings, an absolute artifact URI gets the whole
upload rejected, and a `startLine` of `0` drops the annotation without any
error. `sarif-verify` catches those mistakes locally, in under a second, with
no network access and no runtime dependencies.

```
$ sarif-verify check results.sarif
OK   results.sarif | 0 error(s), 0 warning(s)

$ sarif-verify check broken.sarif
ERROR result-rule-index: ruleIndex 0 points at 'missing-key', not 'empty-value' [runs[0].results[0].ruleIndex]
ERROR uri-relative: uri 'C:/repo/.env' is not repository relative [runs[0].results[0].locations[0].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri]
FAIL broken.sarif | 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)
```

## Why not just use the schema?

A JSON-schema check tells you the document is shaped correctly. It does not tell
you the document will *work*. The checks here encode the code-scanning contract
instead:

| Code | Level | What it catches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `document-type` | error | Top level is not a JSON object |
| `version` | error | `version` is missing or not `2.1.0` |
| `runs` | error | `runs` is missing, empty, or not an array |
| `driver-name` | error | `run.tool.driver.name` is empty (upload rejected) |
| `driver-version` | warning | Tool version missing, so annotations cannot be traced to a release |
| `rules-id` | error | A rule has no usable `id` |
| `rules-duplicate` | error | Two rules share an `id`, making `ruleIndex` ambiguous |
| `column-kind` | warning | `columnKind` outside `utf16CodeUnits` / `unicodeCodePoints` |
| `result-message` | error | A result has no `message.text`, so the annotation renders blank |
| `result-rule` | error | `ruleId` is not declared in `driver.rules` |
| `result-rule-index` | error | `ruleIndex` is out of range or disagrees with `ruleId` |
| `result-level` | error | `level` outside `none` / `note` / `warning` / `error` |
| `result-location` | warning | No location, or no `artifactLocation.uri` |
| `uri-relative` | error | Absolute path, `file://` URI, or `..` traversal |
| `region-lines` | error | `startLine` is not a positive integer, or `endLine` precedes it |

Errors fail the run; warnings fail it only under `--strict`.

## Install

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/sarif-verify.git
# or, from a checkout
pip install -e .
```

Requires Python 3.11+. No third-party dependencies.

## Usage

```bash
sarif-verify check results.sarif                 # one file
sarif-verify check a.sarif b.sarif              # several files, exit 1 if any fails
sarif-verify check results.sarif --strict       # warnings become failures
sarif-verify check results.sarif --json         # machine-readable report
sarif-verify check - < results.sarif            # stdin
sarif-verify checks                             # list every check with help text
sarif-verify version
```

Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` findings, `2` unreadable file or invalid JSON.

### In a GitHub Actions workflow

Run it as the step immediately before the upload, so a malformed log fails with
a readable message instead of an opaque `upload-sarif` error:

```yaml
jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install git+https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/sarif-verify.git
      - run: envscope check --sarif results.sarif      # produces the log
      - run: sarif-verify check --strict results.sarif # fails fast if malformed
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with:
          sarif_file: results.sarif
```

### In Python

```python
from sarif_verify import validate

report = validate(document, source="results.sarif")
if not report.ok:
    fo

> An open-source JavaScript and Python toolkit that captures UTM campaign parameters, generates attributed WhatsApp click-to-chat links, and synchronizes lead events with Google Sheets, GoHighLevel CRM, or outbound webhooks.

---

## The Business Problem

Performance marketers and digital agencies spend thousands of dollars every month on **Meta Ads (Click-to-WhatsApp)**, **Google Search Ads**, and paid social campaigns. 

However, the moment a prospect leaves a landing page and jumps into the WhatsApp messaging interface, **standard analytics break into a complete black box**:

1. **Lost Campaign Context:** Sales reps answering WhatsApp messages have no idea which ad, keyword, or campaign prompted the inquiry.
2. **Attribution Blind Spots:** Advertising algorithms (Meta CAPI, Google Ads Smart Bidding) optimize blindly on button clicks rather than actual qualified conversations or closed revenue.
3. **Disorganized Inbound Volume:** High-ticket leads get lumped together with casual, unqualified queries without CRM lead tagging or offline conversion loops.

---

## The Solution

**WhatsApp Attribution Router** bridges the gap between web analytics and direct chat apps:

- **Client-Side Parameter Capture:** Captures `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_content`, `utm_term`, `gclid`, and `fbclid` with zero third-party cookies or fingerprinting.
- **Dynamic WhatsApp Routing:** Formats official WhatsApp click-to-chat links (`https://wa.me/...`) with prefilled messages referencing the exact campaign name and an opaque lead reference token (`lead_ref`).
- **Parallel Server-Side Dispatch:** Dispatches an event payload via `navigator.sendBeacon` or async fetch to a lightweight Python FastAPI gateway.
- **Downstream Synchronization:** Automatically logs click rows to **Google Sheets**, syncs contacts and attribution tags to **GoHighLevel CRM**, and signs outbound webhooks for agency automations.

---

## Architecture & Data Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Client ["Browser / Landing Page"]
        Visitor(["Visitor arrives via Ad"]) --> Page["Landing Page (with UTM parameters)"]
        Page --> Router["WhatsApp Attribution Router (JS)"]
        Router --> Capture["Capture & Normalize UTMs"]
        Capture --> Storage["Session / Local Storage (Consent-Aware)"]
        Storage --> Click{"Visitor Clicks WhatsApp CTA"}
        Click -->|1. Generate Prefilled URL| WA_App["WhatsApp Mobile / Web App"]
        Click -->|2. Send Event via Beacon| FastAPIGateway["Python FastAPI Gateway"]
    end

    subgraph Backend ["Server-Side Gateway (Python)"]
        FastAPIGateway --> Security["Rate Limiter & 512KB Size Cap"]
        Security --> Dedup["Deduplication Engine (48h Window)"]
        Dedup --> Dispatcher["Integration Dispatcher"]
    end

    subgraph Integrations ["Downstream Marketing Tech"]
        Dispatcher --> GSheets["Google Sheets API v4"]
        Dispatcher --> GHL["GoHighLevel CRM (v2 Contacts)"]
        Dispatcher --> Webhook["Generic Outbound Webhook (HMAC-SHA256)"]
    end

    subgraph Conversion_Loop ["Downstream Conversion Loop"]
        WA_App --> CustomerMsg["Customer Sends WhatsApp Message"]
        CustomerMsg --> SalesRep["Sales Representative Identifies lead_ref"]
        SalesRep --> CRM_Update["POST /api/v1/leads (Status: qualified)"]
        CRM_Update --> GHL
        CRM_Update --> GSheets
    end
```

readme.excerpt:
# SEO Audit and Website Health Checker

An ethical, configurable on-page SEO audit application built with Python and Streamlit. Enter a website URL, and the tool crawls internal pages, checks key on-page signals, and produces a prioritized list of issues with recommendations, a summary dashboard, and CSV export.

## Problem it solves

SEO audits are usually manual, slow, and expensive. This tool automates the first-pass technical audit: it catches missing titles and meta descriptions, duplicate titles, weak heading structure, missing canonical tags, images without alt text, broken fetches, and missing `robots.txt` / `sitemap.xml` — then presents everything in a recruiter-friendly, actionable dashboard.

## Key features

- Crawl accessible internal pages within a configurable limit (BFS with polite delays)
- Analyze page titles, meta descriptions, H1/H2 headings, canonical URLs, and indexability signals
- Detect images missing alt attributes
- Detect duplicate titles and duplicate meta descriptions across pages
- Report fetch failures and HTTP status issues
- Check `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` availability
- Prioritized issue list (critical / warning / info) with explanations and recommended fixes
- Summary dashboard with counts by issue type and category chart
- Export issues to CSV

## Safety and ethics

- Respects `robots.txt`, site terms, crawl limits, and server capacity
- Conservative timeouts, delays, and concurrency (single-threaded polite crawl by default)
- Never bypasses CAPTCHAs, authentication, anti-bot controls, or access restrictions
- Does not claim to measure actual Google rankings — findings are directly observed from the page HTML, and recommendations are clearly marked as recommendations

## Technology stack

- Python 3.11
- Standard library `html.parser` (portable, dependency-light core)
- Requests (HTTP fetching)
- Pandas (reporting/CSV)
- Plotly (charts)
- Streamlit (web UI)

## Folder structure

```
seo-audit-tool/
├── app.py                  # Streamlit application
├── seo_audit/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── analyzer.py         # HTML parsing and issue detection engine
│   └── fetcher.py          # Polite HTTP fetching and crawling
├── tests/
│   └── test_analyzer.py    # Unit tests for the analyzer
├── sample.html             # Sample page for offline experimentation
├── requirements.txt
└── .gitignore
```

## Installation

```bash
python -m venv venv
# Windows: venv\Scripts\activate  |  macOS/Linux: source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Usage

```bash
streamlit run app.py
```

Open the local URL shown by Streamlit, enter a website URL, choose the crawl limit, and click **Run Audit**.

### Offline / sample input

To try the analyzer without a network, run the unit tests (see below) or point the tool at any site you are authorized to audit.

## Testing

```bash
pytest -q
```

Tests cover: missing title (critical), noindex detection, missing alt text, multiple H1 headings, duplicate titles across pages, and aggregate counts.

## Limitations and known issues

- Crawling depends on site availability; heavily JS-rendered pages may yield incomplete HTML
- Redirect chains are reported only as fetch failures in this version (full chain tracing is a future improvement)
- Findings reflect the fetched HTML snapshot, not Google's index or ranking position

## Future improvements

- Redirect-chain tracing
- Word-count and keyword-density heuristics
- Mobile vs desktop viewport checks
- Scheduled audits with historical comparison
- CI via GitHub Actions

- [ecommerce-seo-optimizer](https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/ecommerce-seo-optimizer) — on-page product listing audit and optimization for e-commerce

# PPC Performance Dashboard

An interactive paid-media performance dashboard built with Python, Pandas, Plotly, and Streamlit. Upload a Google Ads / Meta Ads / Bing Ads export, and get normalized KPIs, filters, trend charts, campaign and ad group breakdowns, period-over-period comparison, and CSV export — all in one page.

## Problem it solves

Marketers waste hours stitching CSV exports into Excel to answer simple questions: *"How did CTR change this month?"*, *"Which ad group has the lowest cost per conversion?"* This dashboard answers those questions instantly with consistent KPI definitions (CTR, CPC, CPA, conversion rate) and honest, clearly-labeled derived metrics.

## Key features

- Upload CSV or XLSX exports; column names are normalized automatically (date, campaign, ad group, impressions, clicks, spend, conversions)
- Automatic KPI calculation: CTR, CPC, Cost/Conversion, conversion rate
- Sidebar filters: date range, campaign, ad group
- Trend chart for clicks and conversions over time
- Performance tables and charts by campaign and by ad group
- Period-over-period comparison with absolute and percentage deltas
- Download summarized results as CSV
- Bundled synthetic sample data for an instant demo

## Data expectations

The dashboard expects at least a date column and one or more of: impressions, clicks, spend, conversions. Recognized date column names include `date`, `day`, `Date`. Campaign and ad group columns are optional but recommended. Any numeric column that is missing is treated as zero; derived metrics are never invented — they are computed from the columns actually present.

## Technology stack

- Python 3.11
- Pandas (data processing)
- Plotly (interactive charts)
- Streamlit (web UI)
- openpyxl (XLSX upload support)

## Folder structure

```
ppc-performance-dashboard/
├── app.py                  # Streamlit application
├── data_processor.py       # Normalization, KPI, filter, aggregation, comparison engine
├── tests/
│   └── test_data_processor.py
├── sample_data.csv         # Synthetic demo data (4 weeks, 4 campaigns)
├── requirements.txt
└── .gitignore
```

## Installation

```bash
python -m venv venv
# Windows: venv\Scripts\activate  |  macOS/Linux: source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Usage

```bash
streamlit run app.py
```

Choose **Use bundled sample data** for an instant demo, or upload your own campaign export.

## Testing

```bash
pytest -q
```

Tests cover column normalization, KPI math, campaign filters, date-range filters, aggregation, and period comparison.

## Limitations and known issues

- The comparison assumes calendar-aligned equal-length periods
- Real exports vary by ad platform; unknown columns are ignored (no guessing)
- No multi-touch attribution or incrementality modeling — the dashboard reports platform-reported metrics as-is

## Future improvements

- Budget pacing / burn-rate alerts
- Multi-platform data merge (Google Ads + Meta + Bing)
- Forecasts using simple time-series models
- Scheduled email delivery of the report

## Related projects

# E-commerce SEO Optimizer

A practical tool for e-commerce teams and SEO specialists to audit and improve on-page product listings at scale. Built with Python, Pandas, and Streamlit: upload a product catalog, see every title/description/image/price issue, review keyword-aware suggestions, and export an optimized copy — original columns are always preserved.

## Problem it solves

E-commerce stores often have hundreds or thousands of thin product listings: short titles, missing descriptions, no keywords, broken image references. Fixing them manually in a spreadsheet is slow and error-prone. This tool surfaces the exact problems, proposes concrete title/description improvements using the product's own brand/category/keywords, and produces a safe export for review before applying changes upstream.

## Key features

- Upload CSV or XLSX product catalogs (title, description, price, category, brand, image columns recognized and normalized)
- Audit engine: empty/short/long titles, empty/short descriptions, missing prices, missing or malformed image URLs, duplicate titles
- Severity grading: critical / warning / info
- Suggestion engine: expands short titles with brand/category keywords, generates description copy, records reasons for every change
- Safe apply: writes `optimized_title`, `optimized_description`, `optimized` columns without overwriting originals
- Download the optimized catalog as CSV

## Data expectations

The tool looks for a title column (`title`, `name`, `product`, `product title`) and optional description, price, category, brand, image columns. Unknown columns are ignored. Missing values are flagged, never guessed.

## Technology stack

- Python 3.11
- Pandas (catalog processing)
- Streamlit (web UI)
- openpyxl (XLSX support)

## Folder structure

```
ecommerce-seo-optimizer/
├── app.py                  # Streamlit application
├── optimizer.py            # Validation, suggestion, and export engine
├── tests/
│   └── test_optimizer.py
├── requirements.txt
└── .gitignore
```

## Installation

```bash
python -m venv venv
# Windows: venv/Scripts/activate  |  macOS/Linux: source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Usage

```bash
streamlit run app.py
```

Upload a catalog or use the bundled sample, review the issues and suggestions, then apply and download the optimized file.

## Testing

Tests cover issue detection, suggestion generation, missing-title handling, safe apply behavior, and CSV export.

## Limitations and known issues

- Keyword extraction is heuristic (brand, category, top words); it is not a full SEO content service
- Title length guidance uses common best-practice ranges (20-70 title, 50-160 description) — tune the constants in `optimizer.py` to your vertical if needed

# ai-marketing-growth-os

Agentic marketing intelligence platform — a **virtual digital marketing department**.
Four specialist agents (SEO, Ads, E-commerce, Analytics) read real sample data through
permission-gated tools, produce **structured, evidence-backed recommendations**, deduplicate
and prioritize them into a unified action plan, and route every consequential action through a
**human-in-the-loop approval queue**.

Built on the shared portfolio foundation
[`ai-marketing-shared`](https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/ai-marketing-shared):
Pydantic v2 schemas, tool registry, tracing, cost accounting, eval harness, provider abstraction.

> `docker compose up` runs the full pipeline on sample data and produces evidence-backed
> recommendations in the dashboard — with **zero API keys** and **zero cost**.

## Problem

Marketing teams drown in disconnected dashboards. SEO tells you about rankings, ads tells you
about spend, e-commerce tells you about inventory, analytics tells you about traffic — and a
human has to stitch them together, guess which issue matters most, and risk acting without
evidence. Consequential actions (publishing, budget changes, campaign edits) are rarely gated,
so mistakes are expensive.

## Approach

Growth OS models a marketing department as a set of **tool-using agents**:

- **SEO agent** — crawls + GSC + PageSpeed: broken links, missing meta descriptions, low-CTR
  queries, slow pages.
- **Ads agent** — Google Ads + Meta Ads: CPA over target, low CTR creatives, weak ROAS campaigns.
- **E-commerce agent** — product catalog: stock-outs, reorder points, weak PDP conversion,
  pricing outliers.
- **Analytics agent** — GA sessions + GSC: rising bounce, conversion-rate decline, mobile issues.

Every agent:

1. calls **tools** (never hallucinated numbers) at the lowest permission level required;
2. emits **structured recommendations** conforming to shared `Recommendation` / `Evidence` schemas;
3. records a full **trace** (`AgentRun` with tool calls, latency, cost);
4. is **evaluated** against labeled datasets for factual accuracy, tool-use success,
   recommendation quality, prompt-injection resistance, cost, and latency.

An **orchestrator** deduplicates and ranks the combined recommendations into one action plan,
and every write-type action lands in the **approval queue** (`pending → approved → rejected →
executed → measured`) where a human decides.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Data["data/sample_data (CSV, zero keys)"]
        WC[website_crawl] & GSC[gsc_keywords] & PS[pagespeed] & GA[ga_sessions]
        GAD[google_ads] & MAD[meta_ads] & PC[product_catalog]
    end
    Data -->|tools/| T[ToolRegistry + MCP adapters]
    T --> A[agents: SEO / Ads / E-commerce / Analytics]
    A -->|structured Recommendation| O[orchestration: dedupe + prioritize]
    O -->|ActionPlan| B[backend: FastAPI]
    B --> Q[approval queue]
    Q -->|approve/execute/measure| F[frontend dashboard]
    A -->|AgentRun traces| V[trace viewer]
```

Design decisions and tradeoffs are documented in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Repository layout

```
backend/          FastAPI app + approval queue state machine
agents/           SEO, Ads, E-commerce, Analytics agents
tools/            Tool functions + MCP adapters + registry
orchestration/    Dedupe, priority ranking, unified action plan

evaluation/       datasets/ + pytest suites (6 dimensions)

frontend/         Lightweight dashboard (no build step)
infra/            Dockerfile (multi-stage) + docker-compose.yml
docs/             architecture.md, evaluation.md, cost-controls.md
.github/workflows CI: lint, typecheck, test, eval, docker build
```

# from the parent ai_portfolio directory

readme.excerpt:
# ai-agent-testing-lab

Reusable reliability and evaluation lab for every AI marketing agent in the
portfolio. One harness, seven labeled suites, and a CI integration path that
lets every downstream repository report accuracy, precision/recall,
calibration, cost, latency, and reliability from day one.

Part of the [AI Marketing Engineer Portfolio](../ai-marketing-portfolio-meta/README.md).
Builds on the shared schemas and provider abstraction from
[ai-marketing-shared](../ai-marketing-shared/README.md) and is validated against
the flagship [ai-marketing-growth-os](../ai-marketing-growth-os/README.md).

## Problem

AI marketing agents can look impressive in demos and still be unsafe or
unreliable: they hallucinate numbers, call destructive tools, ignore approval
gates, and fail under adversarial input. Every repository in the portfolio
needed a consistent, evidence-backed way to answer the same questions:

- Did the agent cite real evidence for every recommendation?
- Did it call only the tools it was allowed to call?
- Does it resist prompt injection?
- Is it fast enough, cheap enough, and reliable enough to run in production?

Building a bespoke evaluation suite in every repo would repeat work, drift
apart, and never get compared. The lab exists so evaluation is shared, not
reimplemented.

## Approach

The lab is a thin, dependency-light harness built on the shared schemas:

- **TargetLoader** imports an agent factory from any repo (`module:attr`) and
  validates that it returns `dict[str, agent]` objects with a `run()` method.
- **TestHarness** runs the target through seven labeled suites and produces a
  single `LabReport` with metrics and confusion-matrix details.
- **Reporters** emit JSON, Markdown, and a self-contained HTML dashboard;
  GitHub Actions step summaries are supported for CI.
- **Integration** (`integration/run_lab_eval.py`) is the drop-in script that
  downstream repos add to their workflow to report metrics in CI.

The lab evaluates itself: a known-good `ReliableAgent` must pass every suite,
and a known-broken `BrokenAgent` (hallucinated evidence, forbidden write call,
missing approval gate, random failures) must be caught on every
failure-sensitive suite. If the self-evaluation passes, the lab is proven
effective; if it fails, the lab itself is broken.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Target[Any portfolio repo] -->|pip install -e| TL[TargetLoader]
    TL --> H[TestHarness]
    DS[evaluation/datasets - 7 labeled suites] --> H
    H --> R[LabReport]
    R --> JSON[JSON + Markdown + HTML dashboard]
    R --> CI[CI step summary / thresholds]
    CI -->|PASS / FAIL| GH[GitHub Actions]
    SelfEval[evaluation/run.py] -.reproduces known failures.-> H
```

Layout:

```
ai-agent-testing-lab/
├── lab/                  # harness, metrics, reporters, dashboard, integration, CLI
├── evaluation/
│   ├── datasets/         # seven labeled JSON suites
│   ├── run.py            # self-evaluation entry point
│   └── results/          # generated reports (git-ignored)
├── fixtures/             # known-good / known-broken agents for self-evaluation
├── integration/          # CI template + run_lab_eval.py for downstream repos
├── scripts/demo_eval.py  # quick demo against the fixtures
├── infra/                # Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml
└── .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

## Evaluation Summary

| Suite | What it measures | Metric |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Factual accuracy | recommendation cites expected evidence (source + value range) | hit rate on labeled cases |
| Tool-use | only expected tools are called, with success | tool-use success |
| Recommendation quality | completeness of structured recommendations | quality score |
| Prompt-injection resistance | no forbidden write tool on adversarial input | resistance score |
| Cost | measured cost within labeled cap | cost control |
| Latency | total latency within labeled budget | latency budget |
| Reliability | completion rate over repeated runs | reliability

readme.excerpt:
# AI Search Visibility Auditor

Open-source **GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)** toolkit. In 2026, zero-click searches have reached ~68% and AI Overviews cut click-through rates on top organic positions by ~34%. Ranking #1 is no longer enough — brands must be **cited by AI answer engines**. This tool audits whether your website is ready for that world.

It answers three questions:
1. **Are AI crawlers allowed in?** — robots.txt checks for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended and more.
2. **Do you speak the llms.txt standard?** — detects, validates and generates `/llms.txt` so AI crawlers know what to prioritize.
3. **Is your content structured for AI citation?** — audits answer blocks, question-based headings, FAQ/Article schema and E-E-A-T signals (author, dates, structured body).

Built as a free, open-source alternative to paid AI-visibility tools (SE Ranking ~$129/mo, Semrush ~$139–299/mo, Otterly.AI, Promptwatch).

---

## Features

- **AI crawler access audit** — parses `robots.txt` with standard longest-match precedence, flags crawlers that are disallowed from key paths, distinguishes Google-Extended (Gemini training) from AI Overviews indexing.
- **llms.txt detection, validation and generation** — parses existing files, flags missing titles / duplicate URLs / non-absolute links, and generates a ready-to-publish `llms.txt` from your pages.
- **On-page AI-citation readiness audit** — detects direct answer blocks in the first ~100 words, question-based headings, FAQPage / Article / Organization / Person schema (including `@graph`), author & date signals, and structured body content (lists, tables).
- **Streamlit dashboard** — enter a URL, run the audit, see a prioritized issue list (critical / warning / info), crawler access table, suggested `llms.txt`, and CSV export.
- **Zero heavy dependencies** — stdlib-only analysis engine (urllib + html.parser); Streamlit is the only runtime dependency for the dashboard.
- **Polite fetching** — custom user-agent, timeouts, size limits, small crawl delay.

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/ai-search-visibility-auditor.git
cd ai-search-visibility-auditor
pip install -r requirements.txt
streamlit run app.py
```

Then open http://localhost:8501, enter a URL (e.g. `https://your-site.com`) and hit **Run audit**.

## CLI usage (library)

```python
from geo_audit import fetcher, report

status, robots = fetcher.polite_fetch("https://example.com/robots.txt")
_, llms = fetcher.polite_fetch("https://example.com/llms.txt")
_, html = fetcher.polite_fetch("https://example.com/")

audit = report.run_audit(
    domain="https://example.com",
    robots_text=robots if status == 200 else None,
    robots_status=status,
    llms_text=llms,
    llms_status=200,
    html=html,
)
for issue in audit.sorted_issues():
    print(issue["severity"], issue["code"], "-", issue["message"])
```

## What each check means

| Check | Why it matters in 2026 |
|---|---|
| GPTBot / ClaudeBot / PerplexityBot blocked | AI answer engines can't cite what they can't crawl. |
| Google-Extended blocked | Controls Gemini training only; doesn't block AI Overviews. Blocking by reflex hides content from model training pipelines. |
| `llms.txt` missing | The emerging standard that explicitly guides AI crawlers to priority content (adoption accelerating across major sites). |
| No direct answer block | AI extractors often stop at the first clean answer; burying it costs citations. |
| No FAQ/Article schema | FAQ schema feeds structured Q&A pairs straight into knowledge graphs — one of the highest-impact citation signals. |
| No author / no dates (E-E-A-T) | Anonymous, undated content fails AI quality filters. |

## Project structure

```
geo_audit/
  fetcher.py           # polite HTTP fetching (timeout, size limit, delay)
  robots_analyzer.py   # robots.txt parsing + AI crawler access checks
  llms_analyzer.py     # llms.txt parse / validate /

> **Shared foundation for the AI Marketing Engineer portfolio.** One importable Python package —
> schemas, tooling, observability, cost controls, evaluation, and provider abstraction — reused by
> every repository in the portfolio.

Built by **Muhammad Hamid** to make every downstream AI marketing repo coherent: same Pydantic
schemas, same tool permission model, same tracing, same evaluation harness, same zero-cost demo mode.

---

## Why This Exists

Every repo in the portfolio must produce **evidence-backed recommendations**, use **tools safely**,
enforce **human approval**, expose **observability**, and run with **zero API keys**. Without a shared
foundation, 17 repos would drift into 17 incompatible conventions. `ai-marketing-shared` defines those
conventions **once**:

1. **Structured outputs** — Pydantic v2 schemas with field names matching the master prompt exactly.
2. **Safe tools** — a `Tool` base class with explicit permission levels (`read` / `write` / `external`)
   and a registry that rejects calls below the required permission.
3. **Provider-agnostic** — OpenAI, Anthropic, local HTTP endpoints, and a deterministic mock provider
   (default) so every demo runs at `$0.00`.
4. **Observability** — every run is traced with inputs, tool calls, outputs, cost, latency.
5. **Cost controls** — model pricing tables, ledgers, and budget caps.
6. **Evaluation** — a harness with dataset loaders and metric reporters, wired into CI.

---

## Repository Layout

```
ai-marketing-shared/
├── src/ai_marketing_shared/   # The importable package
│   ├── schemas.py             # Pydantic v2 schemas (Recommendation, Evidence, ...)
│   ├── tools.py               # Tool base class, permissions, ToolRegistry, MCP adapter
│   ├── tracing.py             # Tracer, spans, logging utilities
│   ├── cost.py                # Model pricing, cost accounting, cost caps
│   ├── fallback.py            # Rule-based fallback engine (demo mode)
│   ├── eval.py                # Eval harness: dataset loaders + metric reporters
│   └── providers.py           # OpenAI / Anthropic / local / mock provider abstraction
├── agents/                    # Conventions for agents built on top of this package
├── tools/                     # Conventions for tools built on top of this package
├── data/sample_data/          # Sample facts + example run fixtures
├── evaluation/                # Labeled datasets + pytest evaluation suite
├── tests/                     # Unit tests (>90% coverage on core modules)
├── infra/                     # Dockerfile + docker-compose
├── docs/                      # api.md, architecture.md, evaluation.md, cost-controls.md
└── .github/workflows/ci.yml   # lint → type-check → test → build
```

---

## Quick Start (Zero API Keys)

```bash
pip install -e .
pytest                       # unit + evaluation suites, coverage gate ≥ 90%
```

Run a 10-line demo that produces evidence-backed recommendations with the **mock provider**:

```python
from ai_marketing_shared.fallback import build_default_engine

engine = build_default_engine()
facts = {"campaign": "Summer_Sale", "spend": 9000, "cpa": 115.0, "target_cpa": 50.0, "ctr": 0.008}
for rec in engine.evaluate(facts):
    print(rec.agent, "|", rec.issue, "| confidence", rec.confidence)
```

Expected output (deterministic, zero cost):

```
spend-waste-rule | High CPA (115.0) vs target (50.0): pause or reallocate spend on Summer_Sale | confidence 0.9
ctr-rule | CTR (0.008) is well

> **Diagnostic and audit engine for web conversion tracking (Google Analytics 4, Meta Conversions API, Google Ads Enhanced Conversions).**  
> Detects event duplicate firing, unhashed PII privacy leaks in URL query strings, broken Enhanced Conversions hashing, currency/value anomalies, and iOS/ad-blocker signal loss. Automatically exports ready-to-deploy **Google Tag Manager** custom JavaScript deduplication variables and **Meta CAPI** server remediation payloads.

---

![Conversion Tracking Doctor Audit Preview](docs/report_preview.png)

---

## ⚡ The Problem: Silent Conversion Tracking Breakdowns

Modern digital marketing relies entirely on conversion data feeding automated smart bidding algorithms (Target CPA, Target ROAS, Advantage+). Yet conversion pipelines frequently fail silently:

1. **Phantom Revenue Duplication**: Users reloading thank-you pages re-fire purchase events, inflating reported ROAS by 20% to 50% and triggering aggressive, overpriced bidding.
2. **Unhashed PII Privacy Leaks**: Form builders and campaign redirects leak raw customer emails (`?email=`) and phone numbers into GA4 and Meta Pixel URLs, risking immediate ad account suspension and GDPR violations.
3. **Broken Enhanced Conversions**: Uppercase SHA-256 hashes, un-normalized whitespace, or plaintext strings cause ad platforms to reject customer match keys, wasting attribution recovery.
4. **100x Value Scale Errors**: Passing raw Stripe or Shopify integer cents as whole dollars ($299.90 passed as $29,990.00) completely corrupts automated bidding value models.
5. **Missing Deduplication Keys**: Browser pixel tags firing without matching `event_id` parameters to server CAPI webhooks cause platforms to double-count every single conversion.
6. **Severe iOS / Safari Signal Loss**: Third-party cookie blocking and ad-blockers drop 20%+ of browser conversion hits without server-side CAPI coverage.

**Conversion Tracking Doctor** analyzes raw GA4 client exports and Meta CAPI server logs, audits health with mathematical precision, and generates instant remediation snippets.

---

## 🚀 Key Features

- 🔍 **6 Specialized Diagnostic Engines**:

> **A production-grade, open-source PPC budget leak detector for Google Ads and Meta Ads.**  
> Automatically detects search query bleed, internal keyword cannibalization, junk mobile app placements, geo-location bleed, off-hour dayparting spikes, and runaway smart bidding CPC anomalies. Generates one-click exclusion lists for **Google Ads Editor** and self-contained interactive Tailwind CSS audit dashboards.

---

![PPC Waste Audit Dashboard Preview](docs/report_preview.png)

---

## ⚡ The Problem: Invisible PPC Ad Spend Bleed

Modern paid search and display platforms optimize for inventory monetization, often hiding budget waste inside broad matching, Performance Max black boxes, and multi-network default settings:

1. **Broad Match Query Bleed**: Broad match expansion captures low-intent, non-converting queries (`free`, `login`, `jobs`, `tutorial`).
2. **Internal Keyword Cannibalization**: Multiple campaigns or ad groups bid against each other on the same search queries, driving up your own clearing CPCs.
3. **GDN / PMax Junk Placements**: Display campaigns and Performance Max silently serve impressions on hyper-casual mobile games (`mobileapp::*`) and MFA click-farms with high accidental click-through rates and 0% conversion rates.
4. **Geographic Bleed**: Ads show to users outside your targeted geographies due to Google's default *"Presence or interest"* setting.
5. **Dayparting Waste**: High budget burns between 1:00 AM and 5:00 AM with zero conversions and unstaffed sales teams.
6. **Smart Bidding Runaways**: Automated bidding algorithms aggressively bid on low-intent search terms during inventory spikes without CPC ceilings.

**PPC Waste Detector** parses your raw Google Ads or Meta Ads performance CSV reports and pinpoints every wasted dollar with mathematical rigor.

---

## 🚀 Key Features

- 🔍 **6 Specialized Detection Engines**:
  - `SearchQueryBleedDetector`: Flags negative-intent queries, zero-conversion high-spend queries, and traffic spikes.
  - `KeywordCannibalizationDetector`: Maps internal cross-campaign auction conflicts and calculates wasted delta spend.
  - `JunkPlacementLeakDetector`: Detects spam domains, MFA click-farms, and mobile game app IDs (`mobileapp::*`).
  - `GeoBleedDetector`: Catches impressions and spend occurring outside your target service areas.
  - `DaypartingWasteDetector`: Identifies off-peak hourly budget burns with conversion rates below 10% of account average.
  - `SmartBiddingRunawayDetector`: Detects severe CPC inflation ($>3\times$ median) triggered by unconstrained automated bidding.
- 📋 **Google Ads Editor Ready**:
  - `negative_keywords_editor.csv`: Formatted with `Campaign`, `Ad Group`, `Criterion Type`, `Keyword` for bulk import.
  - `placement_exclusions_editor.csv`: Formatted for instant PMax and GDN placemen

readme.excerpt:
# k8s-ai-bench

`k8s-ai-bench` is a benchmark for assessing the performance of LLM models for Kubernetes related tasks. It evaluates AI agents (like `kubectl-ai`) on their ability to perform real-world Kubernetes operations such as creating deployments, debugging crash loops, and scaling applications.

## 📊 Live Dashboard

See [k8s-ai-bench live leaderboard](https://gke-labs.github.io/k8s-ai-bench/) for the latest benchmark results.

The leaderboard shows run results for widely used proprietary and open models over a few run types:

* **Pass@1**: Can the agent solve the task on the first try? This measures raw capability and immediate correctness.
* **Pass@5**: Can the agent solve the task at least once in 5 attempts? This shows if the agent can eventually find a solution.
* **Pass^5**: Does the agent solve the task every single time? This measures reliability and consistency, which is crucial for autonomous usage.



## 🚀 Quick Start

### 1. Build the Binary
```sh
go build
```

### 2. Run an Evaluation
Run the benchmark against your agent binary. Results will be saved to the `.build` directory.
```sh
# Basic usage
./k8s-ai-bench run --agent-bin <path/to/kubectl-ai> --output-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench

# Run a specific task type (e.g., scaling tasks)
./k8s-ai-bench run --agent-bin <path/to/kubectl-ai> --task-pattern "scale" --output-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench
```

## 🛠 Usage Guide

### `run` Subcommand
The `run` subcommand executes the benchmark evaluations. It creates ephemeral clusters to ensure test isolation. We support two platforms for the test environment: **Kind** (default) and **vCluster**.

**vCluster Prerequisites:**
For a detailed step-by-step guide on setting up and using vCluster, see [vCluster Guide](docs/vcluster.md).

To use `vcluster`, you must have:
* The `vcluster` [CLI](https://www.vcluster.com/docs/vcluster/) installed.
* A running host Kubernetes cluster.
* A kubecontext to connect to the host cluster (passed via `--host-cluster-context`).


```sh
# Run with specific LLM provider and model
./k8s-ai-bench run \
  --agent-bin <path/to/kubectl-ai> \
  --llm-provider gemini \
  --models gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25 \
  --task-pattern fix \
  --output-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench
```

**Common Flags:**
| Flag | Description | Default |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `--agent-bin` | Path to kubectl-ai binary (Required) | - |
| `--output-dir` | Directory to write results (Required) | - |
| `--task-pattern` | RegEx pattern to filter tasks (e.g. 'pod', 'fix') | - |
| `--llm-provider` | LLM provider ID (e.g. 'gemini', 'openai') | gemini |
| `--models` | Comma-separated list of models | gemini-2.5-pro... |
| `--concurrency` | Number of parallel tasks (0 = auto) | 0 |
| `--cluster-provider` | Cluster provider to use (`kind` or `vcluster`) | kind |
| `--host-cluster-context` | Host cluster context for vcluster (Required if provider is vcluster) | - |

### `analyze` Subcommand
Process and summarize results from previous runs.

```sh
# Generate a Markdown report
./k8s-ai-bench analyze --input-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench --results-filepath report.md

# Generate JSONL for visualization
./k8s-ai-bench analyze --input-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench --output-format jsonl --results-filepath site/combined_results.jsonl
```

## 💻 Development Scripts
For a streamlined development loop, use the scripts in `dev/ci/periodics/`:

- **Run Evaluation Loop**: Runs evaluations multiple times to test consistency.
  ```sh
  ./dev/ci/periodics/run-eval-loop.sh --iterations 5 --task-pattern "create"
  ```
- **Run Single Evaluation**:
  ```sh
  TEST_ARGS="--task-pattern=fix-probes" ./dev/ci/periodics/run-evals.sh
  ```
- **Analyze Results**:
  ```sh
  ./dev/ci/periodics/analyze-evals.sh --show-failures
  ```

## 📈 Visualizing Results Locally

The `site` directory contains a static website (Vue.js based) for visualizing benchmark results.

1.  **Generate Data**:
    ```sh
    ./k8s-ai-bench analyze --input-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench --output-format jsonl --result

readme.excerpt:
# ![](static/logo-header.png)

> [!NOTE]
> This project is for demonstration only and is not an officially supported
> Google product.
>
> If you're a Googler using this demo, please fill up this
> [form](https://forms.gle/dJUdMEbUu7k3TmT4A). If you're interested in using our
> hosted version, please fill up this
> [form](https://forms.gle/3AknwhhWv2pWw46Q8).

## Introduction

This project provides a production-quality reference implementation for building
Agentic applications that use [Agents] and [Retrieval Augmented Generation
(RAG)][rag] to query and interact with data stored in Google Cloud Databases.

This demonstration features Cymbal Air, a fictional airline. The application
showcases a customer service assistant that helps travelers manage flights and
find information about San Francisco International Airport (SFO), Cymbal Air's
hub. The agent can answer questions like:

* *Are there any luxury shops in the terminal?*
* *Where can I get coffee near gate A6?*
* *I need to find a gift for my colleague.*
* *What flights are headed to NYC tomorrow?*

[rag]: https://www.promptingguide.ai/techniques/rag
[Agents]: https://www.promptingguide.ai/agents/introduction

## Table of Contents
<!-- TOC depthfrom:2 -->

- [Understanding the demo](#understanding-the-demo)
    - [Retrieval Augmented Generation RAG](#retrieval-augmented-generation-rag)
    - [Agent-based Orchestration](#agent-based-orchestration)
    - [Architecture](#architecture)
- [Deployment](#deployment)
    - [Before you begin](#before-you-begin)
    - [One-Time Database & Tool Configuration](#one-time-database--tool-configuration)
    - [Launch the Toolbox Server Choose One](#launch-the-toolbox-server-choose-one)
    - [Running the Agentic Application](#running-the-agentic-application)
    - [Clean Up](#clean-up)
- [Customizing Your Tools](#customizing-your-tools)

<!-- /TOC -->

## Understanding the demo

### Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)

One of the best tools for reducing hallucinations is to use Retrieval Augmented
Generation (RAG). RAG is the concept of retrieving some data or information,
augmenting your prompt to the agent, and allowing it to generate more accurate
responses based on the data included in the prompt. This grounds the model’s
response, making it less likely to hallucinate. This technique is also useful
for allowing the agent to access data it didn’t have when it was trained. And
unlike fine-tuning, the information retrieved for RAG does not alter the model
or otherwise leave the context of the request - making it more suitable for use
cases where information privacy and security are important.

Cloud databases provide a managed solution for storing and accessing data in a
scalable and a reliable way. By connecting an agent to a cloud database,
developers can give their applications access to a wider range of information
and reduce the risk of hallucinations.


### Agent-based Orchestration

This application uses an Agent-based orchestration model. Instead of a static
chain of calls, the LLM acts as an intelligent Agent that decides which tools to
use and in what order. It is given a set of available tools, each with a
specific function (e.g., `find_flights`, `list_amenities`). Based on the user's
query, the agent reasons about the best tool to use to find the answer. This
"thought process" allows the agent to handle a wider variety of queries and to
break down complex questions into smaller, manageable steps.

### Architecture

![Overview](architecture.svg)

The architecture consists of three main components:
1. **Application** -- The user-facing agentic app that orchestrates the
   interaction between the user and the agent.
1. **MCP Toolbox** -- [MCP Toolbox](https://github.com/googleapis/genai-toolbox)
   is a middleware server that exposes the database operations as a set of
   tools. The LLM agent connects to the Toolbox to execute these tools. This
   provides a secure, scalable, and modular way to manage database interactions.
1
